reviews.review:
This game is incredibly boring with an empty yet grindy start. I was running around doing trash gathering and digging away inside a generic and lazy mine. My brain felt mushy and baffled as how this game received such colourful praise. 

The nicest way I can say about this game that it is probably it's not for me. Just go play something else, Stardew Valley, Coral Island, Field of Mistria, Sun Haven. LITERALLY ANYTHING ELSE

Unfortunately, this game isn't suitable to be sold as-is. It is absolutely overrun with bugs and issues, which is sad, because the game itself is quite good. The deal breaker for me is that it constantly crashes with no warning, no acknowledgement, and no ability to manually save. My game has crashed every 30 minutes or so, even after I've done troubleshooting, fully restarted, etc. When it crashes, it looses all data from the in-game day and there is literally no capacity to save until you go to sleep for the day. 

The real bummer is that *after* I started having this problem I found out that this game is notorious for crashing this way, and the developer doesn't seem to care and has not/will not patch it. Even if they didn't want to dig through the code to find the problems and actually fix them, it would work well enough for them to add a cheap solution like a quick access manual save button, but they don't seem interested in even doing that. 

I have run into a few other bugs as well, but they otherwise wouldn't really bother me, such as occasional lagging and a weird issue where the whole screen goes dark and freezes for a while if you step too close to any body of water. However, like I said, the game itself is really decent! It isn't too hard to get into, the lore is interesting especially for this type of game, and so far the tasks are balanced between challenging and achievable.

The developers have a very bad habit of not fixing old bugs... which is why, despite me actually enjoying the game I can't recommend it until they get better about this. This is a problem for their other games too, they drop support to work on a new project despite some bugs causing straight up crashes... it's scummy and bad. If you want to give this game a try please wait until it's super on sale cause it is NOT a $30 game.

Bugs/Major problems I've seen:
- Crashes. It didn't happen a ton on my PC but happened a whole lot on my Switch version... but the fact that it happened at all is really sucky cause that's a game-breaking bug that really should be addressed. It was passable for me because it didn't happen often and the game saves at the end of each day so you don't lose much but I know it's a deal-breaker for most folks.
- Lag. There was a lot of lag in dungeons and some lag in other places. I'm guessing either the models or particles weren't optimized. I didn't notice it too much outside of certain high-density dungeon encounters but I'm also not super good at noticing smaller chunks of lag.
- Incomplete features. For whatever reason, the museum doesn't fit all the artifacts??? it doesn't have enough space for some types yet too many spots for others... a really annoying oversight for collectors like me and it should've been a VERY easy fix that they just decided not to do -_-. There are a couple other little things but I can't remember them off the top of my head.

That being said, I actually really love this game and its gameplay loop (besides the bugs)! It's very unique and is a very fun spin on the farming/life sim genre.
- There's a lot more focus on mining and material gathering which you then refine into other materials to build stuff. The main storyline is fun and satisfying to finish - there's a good balance of difficulty and production progression.
- Combat is very *meh*. I wouldn't say its horrid, but it's very, very rough around the edges. But combat is more a means to an end for material gathering and isn't a massive slog so that's nice. I am not a stickler for combat though, so if you have strong opinions on combat mechanics you may hate it lol.
- Romance is actually VERY sweet and fun! The characters have a lot of depth and the variety of different dates and activities are very charming and fun. As a stickler for romance in this type of game I give it a solid 9/10. Only problem I have is that if you have kids they're forever babies... which is why I'm knocking off points (after-marriage stuff is very important to me ;-;). But the actual dating and romance stuff really is fantastic besides that.
- The mining mechanic is actually really fun and unique because of the artifact hunting. I LOVE gathering the little pieces and putting them together for the museum while I hunt for materials. You can find small artifacts whole, but other artifacts have to be put together from 2-5 pieces which is VERY fun cause it means you can get some massive artifacts and feel satisfying to complete. Only downside for artifacts is that the museum doesn't actually fit all the artifacts for some reason??? Yet another oversight and one that annoys me to no end... but I gotta give them props for the mechanic itself being fun.

Long story short: the devs need to go back and fix the bugs and museum before I can fully recommend this game to you. It's such a pity that they drop these games to fast cause they're genuinely VERY fun and unique! They've really shot themselves in the foot with this behavior cause it makes them look REALLY scummy... but yeah, if you do wanna buy just wait for a sale cause while it's not worth $30, I'd say in it's current state it's worth like $10 tops.

This is one of those games I desperately wanted to love.

On paper, it has everything I usually enjoy: a cozy post-apocalyptic setting, crafting, relationships, a charming art style, and that slow-burn “build a new life” promise. The community loves it, the reviews are glowing, and everyone talks about its heart and potential. I went in fully prepared to agree with all of that.

And honestly? I really tried.

I gave it time. I pushed past the awkward early hours, told myself the systems would click, that the pacing would improve, that I’d eventually feel that comforting loop everyone talks about. I could see the potential everywhere — in the town layout, in the characters’ backstories, in the idea of rebuilding civilization through craftsmanship. It’s not a bad game by any means.

But no matter how hard I tried, it just never fully landed for me.

The gameplay felt more exhausting than cozy. Crafting, which should’ve been the heart of the experience, often felt unnecessarily time-consuming. Everything I needed to build required everything that I haven’t built yet? It was such a grind! 
Progress felt slow in a way that wasn’t relaxing, but frustrating. 

Social interactions, while charming in concept, never truly made me feel connected. Characters were likable, but I struggled to care deeply about them, and conversations felt repetitive before they felt meaningful. Instead of feeling attached to Portia, I often felt like I was working there rather than living there.

And that’s the thing — I wanted to relax with this game. I wanted it to be my cozy escape. But it kept feeling like effort, like something I had to push myself to enjoy rather than something I naturally gravitated toward.

In the end, I don’t think My Time at Portia is overrated — I genuinely understand why people love it. It clearly has heart, ambition, and a lot of love poured into it. It just wasn’t for me. Sometimes a game can be good, full of potential, widely adored… and still not click, no matter how much you want it to. And that’s okay, not every cozy game is your cozy game.

While I do love this game and had began playing it as addictively as I did with Stardew Valley, I can’t recommend this game at all. This game saves only at the end of the day and doesn’t have an autosave, which is hugely problematic because it keeps crashing. For a game with crafting that's on timers and has you racing across the world map to complete tasks, it’s ridiculous that it doesn’t let you manually save or autosave. This is apparently a big problem and because of the game’s age, it’s no longer being supported. So no fixes. I’ve looked into trying to solve this problem, following a dev’s advice in a post asking for help, but the crashes haven’t stopped. Any other advice is a mod that too is no longer supported, or to buy the sequel which came out in 2023 and was last updated in December 2024. I recommend buying this game when it’s on sale like I did, it is not worth the full price. I’m going to try give it another chance by messing with the specs (which I have already lowered) but I don’t have high hopes. A real shame because I could have loved it as much as I do Stardew.

I've read somewhere that you can fix the problem by sleeping immediately after waking up, essentially wasting a day...which is kind of ridiculous for a game that has been fully released. I definitely wouldn't recommend this at full price.

I only have 6 hours (as of Sept 2025) so take my option with a grain of salt, I've barely touched the surface of this game I feel.

There are some pros and cons, which I am going to list because I think some of the cons need to be reworked.

Pros:
- Crafting, farming, lifestock
- Cozy, indie game with elements of fighting and mining
- Decorate your house and landscape
- Creating relationships with those in town and outside; the little stores and all the options available
- The overall artwork of the game is done very well, does give the sense of living in the future from a days gone past

Cons:
- Why do the days go by so fast? (Is there a setting I missed or...?)
- The character design is different and needs tweaking, especially with our character
- The game as a whole doesn't really give you hints nor any sort of guide as to what you should be doing; except for missions/quests. Not much of a tutorial to get you settled into the game, just throws in you and gives you a few pointers real quick then boom, done.
- Feels like it's a bit difficult to mine and gather materials if I'm on a very strict time limit per day
- The way we have to build is....interesting and some of the mechanics feel like a waste of time. I get the need for some realism, but get rid of any menial steps

So as of Sept 2025 (not sure if I'll be able to change the recommendation option or not) I'm giving this a THUMBS DOWN :(

Disclaimer: This is my opinion; I can’t lie to myself. Whether you like it or not, whether I am in the minority or not, I don’t care.

I’ve played about 20 hours of My Time at Portia and despite my negative review, I’ve enjoyed it so far. There’s a lot to learn, whether it’s crafting, game mechanics, NPC interactions etc. However the story is very slow and honestly not that good in my opinion.
The game runs on a day by day system with a calendar full of events, main quests, and side quests. There are some mini games that I enjoyed and the dating system is creative, at least I haven't seen much like it in other games. I love the mining and ruin system, even though it can take a while to find specific items, progressing deeper into the ruins is both fun and satisfying.
Now why I've put a negative review :
Decorating your house is so clunky that I completely gave up on it. The graphics are pretty basic, and the character designs don’t really stand out either. I really hated the saving system, the game only saves when you go to sleep. Since building things takes such a long time,I often end up spamming the sleep button each day just to move forward, which can make you miss events or rush through parts of the story. There are a lot of bugs and the voice lines often don’t sync with the characters, sometimes their lips don’t move at all. This game offers a lot, but at the same time, it can feel strangely empty from time to time. I would definetly not recommend it at full price, it is not worth it, but if you enjoy life sims and don’t get bored easily, it’s worth picking up on sale !

This game has one somewhat interesting idea: crafting by putting objects into a physical place. Imagine building an iron golem in Minecraft.

Alright, are you done imagining? Because the rest of the game is [i]dreadful[/i]. Those giant towers you see in the logo? They're featureless gray mining caves with randomly placed junk inside. Tunnels not included. You've gotta make your own.

About half of the lines of dialogue in the game are voice acted (at random, not separated by type or context or anything), and about 90% of those sound like the voice actor was completely unaware of the context of the line they were reading.

There's a quest where I'm tasked with helping a rival workshop owner with a recipe. I gather the materials and deliver them and am told that I will receive the recipe in the mail after I sleep. I sleep, and check the mail in the morning. There's a letter that literally just tells me that I got scammed. So far, whatever. This is characterizing the rival workshop owner as a criminal.

But then I find the rival workshop owner in the town hall and talk to them. And without a single dialogue option, they go "oh sorry I'm so sorry about scamming you" and hand me about five times what the materials were worth. So I guess they're-- And then the rival workshop owner, still within the same dialogue sequence, starts insulting me again. So I don't know what the developers were trying to show me other than a mess.

It's a game about how you come into a town that apparently has no connections to any other towns, then have a job that four other people already have and do better than you (three of whom are never named and never appear on-screen), and I don't know how it ends because by the time I finished the bridge to the desert and got yet another featureless area with a few randomly placed trees and rocks, I gave up and played something else.

reviews.review: If you're a feminist, you might want to skip this game—some of the lines could be upsetting. This is a game that’s lenient toward men—forgiving when it comes to their appearance but harsh in the judgment of women’s career choices. The crafting and synthesis mechanics are needlessly tedious. If you’re looking for romance in this game, your options for decent men are extremely limited.
